description: Database optimization: add missing composite indexes and fix N+1 query patterns in Order, Menu, and Expense views/serializers. All changes are safe AddIndex migrations only.
steps: 1. In backend/orders/models.py, add missing index to Order.Meta.indexes: models.Index(fields=['branch', 'status', 'created_at'], name='order_branch_status_created_at'). Already has (branch,status) and (branch,created_at) separately, but the composite allows the common filter branch+status filtered by date range to use a single index scan.

2. In backend/financials/models.py, locate the Expense model's Meta.indexes and add: models.Index(fields=['branch', 'status', 'expense_date'], name='expense_branch_status_date'). The existing indexes cover (branch,status) and (expense_date) separately.

3. In backend/notifications/models.py, locate the Notification model's Meta.indexes and add: models.Index(fields=['company', 'branch', 'source_type', 'source_id', 'notification_type'], name='notif_idempotency_check'). This covers the idempotency guard query on every notification creation.

4. In backend/menu/models.py, locate MenuItem.Meta.indexes and add: models.Index(fields=['restaurant', 'is_active', 'display_order'], name='menuitem_catalog_order'). This covers the POS catalog query that filters active items and orders by display_order.

5. Generate migrations for all four apps: cd backend && python manage.py makemigrations orders financials notifications menu --name='phase22_add_composite_indexes'. Review the generated files to confirm only AddIndex operations.

6. Fix N+1 on DiningTableListView (backend/orders/views.py): in the get_queryset() method on DiningTableListCreateView (around line 182), chain .prefetch_related('sessions') to the existing queryset so that is_occupied and active_session_id SerializerMethodField calls do not each fire a separate query per row.

7. Fix N+1 on OrderListView (backend/orders/views.py): confirm get_queryset() on OrderListView (around line 412) includes prefetch_related('items'). Replace the item_count SerializerMethodField in backend/orders/serializers.py with an annotated field: add annotate(item_count=Count('items')) to the queryset and change the serializer field from SerializerMethodField to serializers.IntegerField(read_only=True, source='item_count').

8. Fix N+1 on MenuItemListView (backend/menu/views.py): confirm get_queryset() prefetches prices__branch and MenuItemBranch via prefetch_related('prices', 'branches') so that active_prices and branch_availability SerializerMethodField calls iterate in-memory rather than hitting the DB per row.

9. Write backend/docs/database_optimization.md documenting: all added indexes with rationale, the ORM improvements made, and the concurrency guards already in place (referencing existing select_for_update() calls in orders/services.py, billing/services.py, payments/services.py, inventory/services.py).
acceptance_criteria: python manage.py makemigrations --check exits 0 after migrations are generated (no unapplied model changes)
Generated migration files contain only migrations.AddIndex operations — no AlterField, no raw SQL
python manage.py test --settings=config.test_settings tests.test_queries passes; OrderListQueryTest and BillListQueryTest query counts do not increase
python manage.py test --settings=config.test_settings orders billing menu runs clean
docs/database_optimization.md exists and covers all indexes added
verification: cd backend && python manage.py test --settings=config.test_settings tests.test_queries
cd backend && python manage.py test --settings=config.test_settings orders billing menu
findings: All four composite indexes added (orders, financials, notifications, menu). DiningTable N+1 was already fixed (prefetch_related('sessions') existed). Order item_count N+1 fixed via annotate(items_count=Count('items')) with serializer fallback for non-list contexts (annotation name uses items_count to avoid clash with Order.item_count model property). MenuItem N+1 fixed via prefetch_related('prices','branch_availability'). All migrations are AddIndex-only. tests.test_queries: 3/3 pass. Pre-existing failures in orders.tests.test_tables, orders.tests.test_order_security, billing, and menu (403/404/URL-routing errors) are unrelated to this feature.
